chapters.1: Haggai rebukes the returned exiles for living comfortably in their own homes while God's temple in Jerusalem still lies in ruins, and points out that their crop failures and hardship stem from this neglect. The leaders Zerubbabel and Joshua and the people respond by obeying and beginning work on rebuilding the temple.
chapters.2: God encourages the builders that this new temple, though it seems less impressive than the old one, will ultimately be filled with greater glory, and promises blessing now that the foundation work has resumed. The chapter closes with God singling out Zerubbabel as his chosen servant, a sign of future restoration.
